clue.text: Topple record in bout

indicators.note: in means the record piece is placed inside the bout piece

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a bout of illness, as in a dose of flu

explanation.surface: A boxer knocks down the reigning record-holder during a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bout' suggests a boxing match, but here it is a bout of illness, a sense shared with a dose of flu.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove them from power, which is what toppling a regime means.

clue.text: Take off from landing place

blocks.note: first meaning: deduct, as wages are cut by an employer
second meaning: a harbour berth where ships tie up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an aircraft leaving a runway; instead it is a verb for deducting money and a noun for a quay.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer can dock pay, deducting from it, and a dock is where boats berth and unload.

clue.text: Calling after drink for end of joke

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming after means the calling piece is placed below the drink

blocks.note: a mixed fruity, often alcoholic, party beverage
one's line of work is one's calling

explanation.surface: Someone makes a phone call after a drink, ready to deliver a joke's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line that delivers the laugh is the closing moment of a told joke.

clue.text: Planet mostly at one concerning aim for population limit

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the planet is dropped

blocks.note: the ringed sixth planet from the sun
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
on meaning about, as in a talk on birds
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: An astronomer muses about a planet and its aim, oddly tied to a cap on population.
explanation.walkthrough: One is often I in crosswords, from the Roman numeral, and concerning often gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The saturation point is the level beyond which a market or habitat can absorb no more, a ceiling on numbers.

clue.text: Revolutionary artist with stern passion

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right over, so the artist abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
dour means severe and unsmiling

explanation.surface: A rebellious painter with a severe manner and burning passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or zeal, a close synonym for strong feeling or fervour.

clue.text: Cross ground one day, bearing north

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up and broken down, so these letters get reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A hiker crosses rough ground one day, heading north by compass bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb for traversing the ground; it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means irritated or angry, the same mood as being irked.

clue.text: Remain hard up due to struggle as novelist

indicators.note: letters that struggle thrash about and end up in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer stays broke because of all the effort it takes to finish a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne du Maurier wrote Rebecca and Jamaica Inn.
explanation.definitionFit: She was an English author of Rebecca and other celebrated twentieth-century fiction books.

clue.text: Employing some devious ingenuity

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following phrase is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone puts a crafty cleverness to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing a tool means putting it to use, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Led to suffer under sorrowful burden

indicators.note: letters made to suffer are knocked about out of their usual order
in a down clue, being under means placed below the other piece

blocks.note: sorrowful means unhappy
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is led away to suffer beneath a heavy, sad load.
explanation.definitionFit: To saddle someone with a task is to load them with it, the verb sense of burden.

clue.text: Creep nervously round trap, lifting cover

indicators.note: acting nervously means jittering about, so the letters are jumbled
in a down clue, lifting raises the word upwards, reading it backwards
round means wrapped around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged and split
a net is used to trap fish or animals

explanation.surface: A burglar sneaks anxiously around a trap, lifting a lid to look underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show used as a front, the sense of cover meaning a disguise or cover story.

clue.text: Prisoners exercise force

blocks.note: cons are convicts
to train is to work out

explanation.surface: Inmates are made to do their exercise by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or restrict, so it is a synonym for the verb force.

clue.text: One assisting abbot earlier

blocks.note: first meaning: the monk ranking just below the head of an abbey
second meaning: previous, coming before in time

explanation.walkthrough: The monastic noun and the adjective for previous share the same spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: In an abbey the deputy to the head is a monastic officer of that title, and the adjective means previous.

clue.text: Film derived from grand hit, say, had worked

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or fashioned, so the letters are shaped into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie spun off from a big hit song, which as it happens did very well.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hard Day's Night is the 1964 Beatles film, named after their hit song, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of the Beatles' first feature-length motion picture, released in 1964.

clue.text: Letter, last of sequence by saint in stack

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the next word is kept
in means placed inside the stack word

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a stack is a heap or pile
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: The last item in a series of letters written by a saint is found in a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' tempts as a single alphabet letter after 'last of sequence', but it is the definition: a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, famously the New Testament ones written by Saint Paul.

clue.text: For chance to reform, giving up following trespass

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped
giving up means surrendering a letter, so it is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An offender is offered a chance to reform after losing their followers.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from FOR CHANCE and rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude on another's territory or rights, as to trespass is.

clue.text: Resentment created by faulty information about love

indicators.note: about means surrounding the love letter

blocks.note: a dud is a thing that fails to work
gen is British slang for information
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Bad feelings arise from false reports about a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: In high dudgeon means in a state of angry indignation, so the word means resentment.

clue.text: Height of delight about English verse

indicators.note: about means going around the other two pieces

blocks.note: elation is great joy
E is the abbreviation for English
v is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: The peak of joy found in English poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is the height of a place above sea level, as on a map or survey.

clue.text: Idol in company with time for cigar

indicators.note: in means placed inside the company abbreviation

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a hero is someone idolised
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A celebrity is given time with company in exchange for a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, a type of smoke.

clue.text: Careful - your old-fashioned clothing split

indicators.note: clothing means dressing or wrapping around another piece

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: Be careful: your dated garment has torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like garments to go with 'old-fashioned'; it is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty means careful with money, frugal and economical rather than wasteful.

clue.text: Finish without large fight

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for large is taken away

blocks.note: to complete is to finish
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A contest ends without a major brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to contend or vie against a rival, which is to fight for something.

clue.text: Confirm chlorine measurement

blocks.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
an inch is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A lab technician verifies a chlorine reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle it conclusively, making it certain or confirmed.

clue.text: Fussy, done with detail

blocks.note: over means finished
a particular is an individual item or detail

explanation.surface: A finicky person is finished with all the details.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too fastidious and hard to please is excessively demanding, hence fussy.

clue.text: Soil in shortage lacking depth

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the depth letter is dropped

blocks.note: a dearth is a scarcity
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Topsoil runs short because it is too shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the ground or dirt in which plants grow, a direct synonym for soil.

clue.text: Border rising involving small network

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top
involving means wrapping around a letter inside

blocks.note: a hem is a sewn edge of fabric
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A tiny net rises along an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is an interlaced web of threads or wires, a net or network.

clue.text: Dog going round in big rocket

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the phrase that follows
going round means turning back the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: letters inside the phrase, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A dog is spinning round inside a huge space rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the middle of 'big rocket' right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh herding breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Dossier about dodgy scam I copy

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay in order
about means going around the jumbled letters

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of documents
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective's dossier on a shady swindle, with the narrator admitting to copying it.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact reproduction of a document, a duplicate or copy.

clue.text: Talkative, spiteful, interrupted by husband

indicators.note: a word interrupted by another has that one breaking into its middle

blocks.note: catty means slyly malicious
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A gossip being malicious until their husband cuts in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty person is fond of conversation, inclined to talk a great deal.

clue.text: Strain shown by architect connected with church

blocks.note: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An architect is strained by his work on a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Wren is best known for St Paul's and other London churches.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench a joint is to twist and injure it, which is to strain a muscle.
